summary: Figure 5 contrasts two GPU server interconnects that BlitzScale's network model must account for. Both panels share the same template: a row of GPUs in Server 0 feeding a NIC and CPU memory, linked to Server 1 over a 200 Gbps RDMA network, whose own NIC feeds Server 1's GPU row. The panels differ only in what joins the GPUs within Server 1. In (a) A800 SXM, each GPU has its own NVLink port feeding a shared NVSwitch, giving 1.6 Tbps of GPU-to-GPU bandwidth. In (b) A100 PCIe, there is no NVSwitch; instead a looping connector shows that GPUs 0 and 1 simply share one 256 Gbps PCIe link. The comparison makes the point that without NVLink, intra-server GPU bandwidth collapses from terabit-scale to a PCIe link only about as fast as the inter-server RDMA network.
